summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM applications move into production, with New Relic reporting 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in AI monitoring adoption. These tools help teams trace workflows, evaluate output quality, detect hallucinations, track token costs, and connect AI issues to broader application performance. Choosing the right tool depends on your stack, budget, volume, and preference for open-source versus managed solutions.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, chains, agent workflows, output quality, token usage, and latency — deeply integrated with the LangChain ecosystem.
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month with overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention (~$264 at 100,000 traces). Trace costs can reach 5–10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain/LangGraph that want deep, first-party observability and evaluation tooling.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, cost, latency, and usage across 300+ models — operates as a lightweight proxy/gateway.
features: Single-line base URL integration (setup in under 5 minutes)
Cost tracking via a 300+ model cost repository
tools.pricing: Free up to 10,000 requests/month; Pro reportedly reaches the 100,000-trace milestone around $79 — a fraction of comparable LangSmith costs.
tools.best_for: Teams needing fast, low-overhead cost governance and visibility into spend across many models without framework lock-in.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiments, model performance, evaluations, and the broader ML/AI development lifecycle.
features: Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Integration with training and fine-tuning workflows
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans are consumption/seat-based with custom enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams that want unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability across the full model lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Model drift, embeddings, LLM traces, RAG quality, and evaluation metrics — with strong OpenTelemetry integration.
features: Open-source Phoenix for tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AX managed/enterprise platform offers custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams focused on model drift detection, embedding analysis, and standards-based (OpenTelemetry) observability.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, cost tracking, online evaluations, and usage analytics — available open-source and self-hostable.
features: Cost and token tracking per trace
tools.pricing: Open-source self-hosting is free (infrastructure costs only); managed cloud offers a free tier with usage-based paid plans — popular as a cost-effective alternative for high-volume deployments.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, cost-controllable observability platform they can self-host at scale.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, and latency using OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation that exports to existing observability backends.
features: Vendor-neutral — exports to Datadog, Grafana, New Relic, etc.
Integrates with existing enterprise observability stacks
tools.pricing: Open-source and free; costs are determined by the backend observability platform you export telemetry to.
tools.best_for: Teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation plugged into their existing enterprise observability tooling.

cost_tips: Use a proxy/gateway like Helicone to cache repeated responses and attribute spend per user or department — enabling cost governance without heavy integration.
Match the model to the task: route simple queries to smaller, cheaper models and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning, using multimodel routing tools like Portkey.

Watch observability overhead itself — LangSmith trace costs can reach 5–10% of underlying LLM API spend, so consider self-hosting Langfuse or request-based pricing (Helicone) for trace-heavy, high-volume workloads.
Reduce token consumption by trimming prompt context, compressing system prompts, limiting max output tokens, and leveraging prompt caching and retrieval that returns only the most relevant chunks.
